concept.name: Diamond top
concept.definition: A rare classical reversal pattern at the end of an uptrend whose outline resembles a diamond — often tilted — formed by an initial broadening phase (higher peaks and lower valleys) followed by a contracting phase (lower peaks and higher valleys, like a symmetrical triangle). The conventional expectation is a downward breakout reversing the prior rise. It is a technical-analysis hypothesis, not a proven predictive law.
concept.intuition: Volatility first explodes outward and then collapses inward, as if the market thrashed itself into exhaustion; the diamond's tip marks where the uptrend's energy runs out.
concept.mechanics: Draw trend lines connecting the peaks and valleys: diverging in the first half, converging in the second; price should touch each boundary once or twice and volume trends downward roughly 55–59% of the time. Breakouts are downward about 54% of the time in Bulkowski's sample, confirmed by a close outside a boundary. The measure rule projects the pattern's height (highest peak minus lowest valley) from the breakout; after a quick vertical rise into the diamond, price often returns near the launch level.
concept.formula: Price target = B +/- (P - V), where B = breakout price, P = highest peak in the diamond, and V = lowest valley (sign follows breakout direction).
concept.failure_modes: Diamonds are hard to identify correctly (often skewed, with outliers hiding the shape), and Bulkowski ranks upward breakouts from diamond tops last of 39 patterns for performance — expecting continuation up from this 'reversal' pattern is the weakest bet. Pullbacks after the breakout frequently bust the signal.
concept.misconceptions: That a diamond top must resolve downward — the downward bias is only about 54%, barely better than chance, so the breakout direction, not the label, should drive action.
concept.example: After a near-vertical rise from $20 to $35, a stock's swings widen then narrow into a tilted diamond around $30–$36; a close below the lower-right boundary near $31 triggers the measure rule toward the high $20s, near the rally's launch point.
